causal_chain.weakest_link: molecular_function->process, which is empty of experiment. The transport function is solid but entirely from mammalian orthologs read as abstracts, and nothing bridges 'moves leucine/methionine' to 'changes fin ray length'. A second, nearly as bad break: all six ZFIN rows and every phenotype statement come from one publication (ZDB-PUB-210918-31 / PMID 34534441), so this gene has no independent replication.
gaps: No pathway or process step for Lat4a in the fin: no mTOR/mTORC1 readout, no amino acid measurement in fin tissue, no substrate rescue, no transcriptional target.
Zebrafish Lat4a transport activity has never been measured; the molecular function is imported from human/mouse orthologs.
No cell type resolved for lat4a in the fin (no transplantation, no clonal mosaic, no cell-type driver).
Direction of the T200K effect on transport is unknown: the allele is a genetic gain of function but no transport assay was done on it, so whether it moves more or less amino acid is undetermined.
Every fin phenotype and every ZFIN row for this gene traces to a single paper (PMID 34534441); no independent replication was found.
Flying-fish Lat4a (F326L) was never functionally tested in any species; it is a convergent substitution in a sequence alignment.

gaps: Stewart 2021 (PMID 34061172) full text unavailable: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 for PMC8217709 and NCBI PMC efetch returned a publisher 'does not allow' notice. All Stewart 2021 statements here are abstract only.
Zero ZFIN phenotype rows for kcnh2a; no ontology-term phenotype annotation to cite.
No measurement of membrane potential, intracellular K+ or Ca2+ in a kcnh2a-expressing fin cell.
The clone-autonomy sufficiency experiment in Daane 2021 used human KCNH2, not zebrafish kcnh2a.
No kcnh2a functional data in any flying fish: the flying-fish evidence for this locus is comparative-genomic only.
